summary: The 2006 series' first 50 rows adapt manga chs 1-44 with two deliberate reorderings and three anime-original blocks between them. Rows 1-13 run chs 1-28 but move the Introduction arc's second half OUT of order: ep 2 jumps to chs 5-7 (arrival at the Order) after quoting two pages of ch 2, eps 3-5 take the Ghost of Mater arc (chs 8-16), and only then do eps 6-7 go back and adapt chs 2-4 (Jan/Leo and the Mana flashback) — dgrayman.fandom's Introduction Arc box states this outright ('chapter 1-7 / episode 1-2 and 6-7') and the ep-6 page notes 'in the manga, this arc takes place before the Ghost of Mater Arc'. Rows 19-24 adapt the Krory arc straight (chs 31-42), and only afterwards does ep 26 (stored mixed) reach back to ch 29 — the anime turned General Yeegar's fall, which is already past tense in the manga, into an on-screen event told AFTER the Krory arc. So three anchors are non-monotonic by design (eps 6, 7, 26) and carry `rearranged`. Rows 37-40 are the anime's stretched version of ch 43-44: only eps 38-39 carry first-time manga pages (ep 39 matches ch 44 beat for beat — 148 caskets, 6 Exorcists and 142 Finders, Suman Dark missing), while ep 37 is Daisya's anime-original origin story and ep 40 is the opening of the anime-original Lulu Bell arc; both are anchor_hostile (A44) and ep 28 turns out to be pure filler despite AFL/AFG typing it Manga Canon. Ch 30 ('Missing in Action') is never adapted straight by either series — its beats are redistributed into eps 37 and 39. The upper fence is repaired: ep 51 reaches ch 46 (pp 2-10), not ch 45. Surprises: eps 29-30 and 33-34 adapt the licensed D.Gray-man Reverse light novels (a side_source shape, flagged), and the anime-original ep 36 grafts fragments of chs 41, 42 and 43 while carrying no plot of its own.

anchors.note: Ch 1 'Opening' (Moore Hesse, the haunted church, Marc) — the whole 57-page opening chapter is this episode; A4/A10 both land on 1.

Arrival at the Black Order = chs 5-7 (ep title 黒の教団 = ch 5's title, en-WP chapter list). The 2 pages lifted from ch 2 are a relocated fragment, so A10 (≤5 pages) and A12 keep START at 5; the rest of ch 2 waits for ep 6 — see the rearranged annotation.
Ghost of Mater arc opens (chs 8-16 = eps 3-5 per the arc box); ch 10 is split with ep 4 (the ch-10 page lists eps 3 and 4).
Ep title 土翁と空夜のアリア is the shared title of chs 9-16 (en-WP/ja-WP); chs 10 and 13 are each split with the neighbouring episode per the chapter pages.
Closes the Mater arc at ch 16 (Lala/Guzol). Frontier of the block so far — eps 6-7 then drop back to chs 2-4 (A4 running order).

REARRANGED (A4, 'pages, not numbers'): the episode's first-time pages are ch 2 from p6 and ch 3 pp3-14 (Jan, Leo, the Earl) — material the manga places BEFORE the Mater arc. The 20-page lead-in of ch 2 is well over the A10 sliver bar, so START = 2. Anchor sits behind ep 5's by design.

REARRANGED: finishes ch 3 (10 pages, over the A10 bar → START 3) and adapts ch 4, closing the Introduction arc's displaced half; Lenalee's presence in the graveyard is an anime addition (in the manga Allen has not yet reached the Order).
Ep title 黒の教団壊滅事件!? is chs 17-18's title (en-WP); the whole Komurin mini-arc is this one episode (arc box: chs 17-18 = ep 8).
Ep title 巻き戻しの街 = ch 19's title; stops 7 pages into ch 20, which ep 10 finishes (ch-20 page lists eps 9 and 10).
Picks up ch 20 mid-chapter (12 pages, over the A10 bar → START 20) and runs through ch 22 'Human'.
Chs 23-24 in full; ch 25 'Regenerate' only p1 and pp5-6 here — the rest is held for ep 12 (rearranged annotation). END is the furthest first-time chapter = 25.
Ep title そして街に雪が降り… = ch 26's title 街に雪が降り (en-WP); ch 25's remaining pages open the episode, so START = 25 (well over the A10 bar).

Ep title 団服と共に carries ch 28's title 団服 (en-WP); chs 27-28 (Bookman/Lavi, the coat lesson) complete the pre-filler run. Ch 29's opening pages (the rubble, Bookman's interrogation) are NOT here — the anime redistributes them to eps 25-26.
Ep title 古城の吸血鬼 = ch 31's title 孤城の吸血鬼① (en-WP); the Vampire arc opens (arc box: chs 31-41 = eps 19-24). Note the anime skips past chs 29-30 to get here — see the ep-13 continue point.
Chs 32-33 in full and into ch 34, which the ch-34 page splits between eps 20 and 21.
Ch 34's remainder through ch 37 'Merge' (ch 37 is split with ep 22). END chapter 37 opens volume 5 (en-WP volume list).
Ep title エリアーデの真実 covers ch 38 'Broken Hearts, Broken Roses'; ch 37's tail opens the episode (ch-37 page lists eps 21 and 22).
Chs 39-40 ('Affection' / 'A Reason') — Eliade's death; both chapter pages name ep 23 alone.

The episode-page chapter field is EMPTY, but the ch-41 and ch-42 pages both name ep 24 and the content is beat-for-beat (Krory on the train, Allen's strip-poker win against Tyki's group, Tyki meeting the Earl). The HQ arrival that closes the episode is an anime bridge into the filler block. Frontier of the block until ep 38.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 29 (the Earl's 'the prologue is over' message and Komui's/Bookman's explanation of the Heart; the episode page pins pp 12-13)
anchors.note: REARRANGED + the row's canon share as stored mixed: ch 29 'Crisis of the Generals' is the only manga in the episode — Yeegar's on-screen battle with Road and Tyki is anime-original (in the manga he is already dead and mad before ch 29 opens; the fandom episode note says so). Anchor sits behind ep 24's 42 by design; ch 29 is the furthest FIRST-TIME chapter here.

The episode page's chapter field is empty; the ch-43 page names eps 36 and 38-39 and the Order in Crisis arc box gives chs 42-45 = eps 36-39. Content is decisive for ch 43's first-time pages: Kanda/Marie/Daisya splitting up and agreeing to regroup at dawn, and the wall caving in as Daisya walks out in front of Tyki. Everything else (the Finders' defence of Barcelona, Tiedoll's wagon family) is anime-original padding.

Ch 43's ending (Daisya crucified on the lamppost) then ch 44 almost page for page: Tiedoll burning the drawing of Bodrum and refusing to return, Komui before the 148 caskets, 6 Exorcists and 142 Finders dead, the identical cause of death, Suman Dark missing, Komui refusing to return the remains. The ch-44 page names eps 39 and 51. Furthest first-time chapter of the whole 1-50 block.

continue_points.note: Read on at ch 5 (the Black Order): chs 2-4 are held back and animated out of order in eps 6-7, so skipping them here keeps you level with the anime.
Ep 2 borrowed only 2 pages of ch 2; chs 2 (from p6) to 4 arrive in eps 6-7. Continue at ch 8, where ep 3 starts (C2 parity).
Everything through ch 16 is animated; chs 2 (p6 on)-4 are still owed and eps 6-7 deliver them next. Continue at ch 17 (C2 parity — do not read back).
Ep 6 is the anime catching up on ch 2-3; the reading frontier is unchanged at ch 17.
With chs 2-4 finally animated, chs 1-16 are complete and ep 8 starts at ch 17 — read on there (C2).

Eps 14-18 are anime-original; the next adapted episode (19) starts at ch 31. Chs 29-30 are skipped here — ch 29 is animated later and out of order in eps 25-26, and ch 30 'Missing in Action' is never adapted straight by either series, so read it when you like (C2/C3).
Chs 31-42 are now animated; ch 29 is still owed (ep 26 tells the Yeegar arc out of order) and ch 30 is never adapted. The next first-time coverage is ep 38 at ch 43 — continue there (C2).

Ep 26 closes the out-of-order ch 29; only ch 30 remains unanimated behind the frontier (never adapted — read it here if you want it). Eps 27-36 are anime-original/novel adaptations; ep 38 resumes the manga at ch 43.

Ep 39 finishes ch 44 except its last page (Suman's eyes watching Allen), which ep 51 re-shows as its cold open. Eps 40-50 are the anime-original Lulu Bell arc; ep 51 starts the manga again at ch 45, so continue at 45 (C2 parity — the re-shown ch-44 page is not a new position).

anchor_hostile.why: 'Exorcist Krory' (Krory's first solo mission, the stained-glass Innocence, the friendly Level 2 Akuma) has no counterpart anywhere in the manga: no chapter page in chs 27-56 names ep 28, the episode page carries no chapter field and puts the row in the Second Filler Arc, and the arc page lists 'Episodes 27-28: Filler Stories 1'. A44/A1 — position-less; type repair to filler proposed below (AFL and AFG both type it Manga Canon, which is wrong).

The episode's job is Daisya Barry's anime-original origin story (Bodrum, the family doorbell that becomes Charity Bell, Tiedoll's recruitment) — roughly three quarters of the runtime. Its manga tie is a loose parallel only: Kanda and Daisya fighting Akuma on the way to Barcelona echoes ch 30's opening and ch 43's opening, and ep 38 adapts those pages in place. No first-time source pages of its own → A44 position-less (see the loose_parallel annotation). The row's TYPE is contested — see flags.

'Requiem Rose' (Rose Valley, the Rosedolina festival, the Earl dispatching Lulu Bell) is the opening episode of the anime-original Lulu Bell's Attack arc — dgrayman.fandom's arc page gives that arc as episodes 40-50 and narrates ep 40's plot inside it, the episode page carries no chapter field, and the manga's own Order in Crisis arc is bounded at ep 39. The only manga content is Lavi verbally recapping ch 44's casualty report, which ep 39 already animated — re-shown material is never a position (A44/'pages, not numbers'). Type repair to filler proposed below.

annotations.note: The Introduction arc's second half is told out of order: ep 2 lifts only ch 2 pp4-5 and jumps to chs 5-7, and chs 2 (from p6) to 4 are animated after the Mater arc, in eps 6-7 ('in the manga, this arc takes place before the Ghost of Mater Arc' — fandom ep-6 note; Introduction Arc box: chs 1-7 = eps 1-2 and 6-7).
Ch 25 'Regenerate' is split: ep 11 closes on p1 and pp5-6, ep 12 takes the remainder.
Ch 34 is split down the middle between eps 20 and 21 (both chapter- and episode-page fields agree).
Ch 37 'Merge' is split between eps 21 and 22.

Filler row (A1, no anchor): the anime-original Yeegar mission quotes ch 29 — the episode page pins 'ch 29, page 6' and the ch-29 page names eps 25 and 26. The Komui/Bookman exchange about Allen's cursed eye also echoes ch 41's opening phone call.
Ch 29 is animated AFTER the Krory arc (chs 31-42, eps 19-24), so ep 26's anchor sits behind ep 24's — the block's one deliberate backward step in the second half.

Yeegar's on-screen fall — Allen's meeting with him, the fight with Road and Tyki, the Dream World torture — is anime-original; the manga has him already dead and mad before ch 29 opens, with Komui delivering the news. The canon share is the Earl's 'prologue is over' message and the explanation of the Heart.

Filler row (A1, no anchor): the anime-original Finder episode quotes Lenalee's nightmare of the ruined Order (ch 41), Tyki's life with Eeez/Klack/Momo and the keepsake taken from Yeegar (ch 42), and the Noah luncheon with Road's homework and the Earl dealing out target cards (ch 43). The ch-43 page names ep 36; the episode carries no plot of the source.

Kanda and Daisya fighting Akuma en route to Barcelona restages beats from ch 30's opening (the Tiedoll unit hunting their general) and ch 43's opening (Daisya's Charity Bell); ep 38 adapts those pages properly. Daisya's childhood is anime-original.
Ch 43 (17 pages) is stretched across two episodes with heavy anime-original padding — the Finders' defence of Barcelona, Giscone's unit, Tiedoll and the Vilanova family, Devon's death.
The only manga content is Lavi restating ch 44's casualty report (148 coffins, cremation without notifying families) that ep 39 already animated — re-shown material, not a position.

Ep 51 opens on ch 44's last page (the eyes watching Allen from the tree — Suman, per the Gray Log fanbook) before running chs 45-46; that page belongs to ep 39's coverage, so it does not move the position.

repairs.why: The stored value is the batch-6 LOW-MED estimate ('Edo departure ≈ ch 45'). The episode page lists 'Chapter 44 (page 16), Chapter 45 (pages 1-10), Chapter 46 (pages 2-10)' and BOTH the ch-45 and ch-46 pages name eps 51 and 52 — so ep 51's furthest first-time mainline chapter is 46, not 45 (A4). START stays 45 (ch 44's single last page is a sliver under A10/A12); chapters_adapted should read '44 (p16), 45 (p1-10), 46 (p2-10)', volume 5. The stored continue 45/parity remains correct (ep 52 restarts inside ch 45), and the existing partial{45-46} annotation on eps 51-52 is unaffected.
END ch 46 is the last chapter of volume 5 (en-WP volume list, matching the stored boundary v5: 37-46).

type_corrections.note: Stored canon (AFL and AFG both say Manga Canon) but the episode adapts nothing: Krory's first solo mission with Lavi, Bookman and Toma, the village with Innocence hidden in a stained-glass window and the two-faced Level 2 Akuma appear in no chapter. dgrayman.fandom files it under the Second Filler Arc with an empty chapter field and its arc page lists 'Episodes 27-28: Filler Stories 1'; no chapter page in the surrounding space (chs 41-46) names ep 28; a 2008 JP fan breakdown independently says '28話もオリジナル'. T28: the episode's job is an original episodic story, so the row is filler and takes no anchor (A1).

Stored canon (AFL/AFG: Manga Canon) but 'Requiem Rose' is the first episode of the anime-original Lulu Bell's Attack arc — dgrayman.fandom's arc page defines that arc as 'the third filler arc of the anime … episode 40-50' and its summary is ep 40's plot; the episode page has no chapter field; the manga's Order in Crisis arc box stops at ep 39. Its only manga material is a verbal recap of ch 44 already animated in ep 39. T28: original plot quoting an already-adapted fragment → filler with a loose_parallel tie, no anchor (A1).

structure.notes: ROW IDENTITY (checked first): our rows 1-50 match AFL, AFG, ja-WP 各話リスト and the French wiki on title AND air date one-for-one (ep 1 = 2006-10-03 … ep 50 = 2007-09-18); AFL's type column equals our stored types on every row in the range, so no index join was needed anywhere (R20 — all joins were by title/chapter title). CHAPTER SPACE: the manga's own chapter ('Night') numbering; en-WP's chapter list reproduces the stored volume boundaries exactly (v1 1-7, v2 8-16, v3 17-26, v4 27-36, v5 37-46, v6 47-56), and AniList's 258 is the same space. ORDER: the 2006 series reorders twice — (a) the Introduction arc's second half (chs 2-4) is moved behind the Ghost of Mater arc into eps 6-7, and (b) the General Yeegar arc (ch 29) is moved behind the Krory arc (chs 31-42) into eps 25-26. Consequence: THREE anchors in this block are non-monotonic by design (ep 6 → 3 and ep 7 → 4 after ep 5 → 16; ep 26 → 29 after ep 24 → 42), each carrying `rearranged`; the reader-facing position is carried by the continue points (17, 17, 43), not by the anchors. NEVER ADAPTED: ch 30 'Missing in Action' — no chapter page assigns it to any episode and neither the 2006 series nor HALLOW stages it; its beats are scattered into ep 37 (the Tiedoll unit hunting their general) and ep 39 (Timcanpy leading the way to Cross). Chs 29-30 are the only pre-ch-45 gap left by the whole block. NOVEL ADAPTATIONS INSIDE THE FILLER RUN: eps 29-30 adapt Reverse vol 1 ch 1 'The Traveling Clergyman' and eps 33-34 adapt Reverse vol 1 ch 2 'The Village Where the Witch Dwells' (Kaya Kizaki / Shueisha, illustrated by Hoshino) — the same licensed-second-work shape as Black Clover 55-56; flagged rather than retyped because they sit outside this lane's target rows. SOURCE BEHAVIOUR: dgrayman.fandom is internally consistent in both directions here — every episode page's `chapter(s)` field agrees with the matching chapter page's `episode(s)` field for chs 1-46 — but the fields are EMPTY (not zero) on eps 24, 36, 38, 39 and 40, so absence there is not evidence; the arc boxes give chapter↔episode ranges at arc granularity only (the Order in Crisis box's 'episode 36-39' includes the filler ep 36 and the hostile ep 37). AFG's D.Gray-man page reproduces AFL's typing exactly and is not independent of it.

flags_for_sean: ep 37 TYPE is contested and I did not repair it: dgrayman.fandom's Second Filler Arc page lists 'Episodes 35-37 Filler Stories 3' and a 2008 JP fan breakdown says Daisya's past was invented for the anime, but the same wiki's Order in Crisis arc box says 'episode 36-39' and AFL + AFG both type it Manga Canon. Delivered as anchor_hostile (A44) with a loose_parallel{30,43} annotation either way. If you retype it filler, nothing else in this verdict changes. https://dgrayman.fandom.com/wiki/Second_Filler_Arc | https://dgrayman.fandom.com/wiki/Order_in_Crisis_Arc | https://www.animefillerlist.com/shows/d-gray-man

SIDE_SOURCE candidates outside the target rows: eps 29-30 are 'loosely based on the light novel The Travelling Clergyman' and eps 33-34 are explicitly tagged as adapting 'The Village Where the Witch Dwells (novel chapter)' — both are chapters of D.Gray-man Reverse vol 1 (Kaya Kizaki, Shueisha, Hoshino illustrations). That is the Black Clover 55-56 shape (canon + side_source naming the work, no chapter anchor by design), and the ep pages list the novel-vs-anime differences in detail. Stored type is filler on all four; a 2008 JP fan answer independently says '29,30話は小説のお話' and '33,34話も小説の話'. Not retyped here — outside lane A2's target rows and 'loosely based' may not clear your adaptation bar. https://dgrayman.fandom.com/wiki/Episode_29 | https://dgrayman.fandom.com/wiki/Episode_33 | https://dgrayman.fandom.com/wiki/D.Gray-man:_Reverse

NONMONOTONIC by design: eps 6, 7 and 26 anchor behind their predecessors (3, 4 and 29 against 16 and 42). This is the batch-19 `rearranged` shape, not a defect, but it will light up any monotonicity audit for d-gray-man rows 1-26; the continue points (ep 5/6/7 → 17, ep 24/26 → 43) carry the honest reader position across the dip.

Page-split completeness: the wiki's page pins are not exhaustive — ch 3 pp1-2 and ch 21 p19 are named by no episode, and the ch-29 pins ('p6' for ep 25, 'pp12-13' for ep 26) account for only a fraction of a 17-page chapter. The chapter NUMBERS are solid; treat the page strings in chapters_adapted as the wiki's pins, not a full page map.

ep 38's anchor is medium: its episode page has an empty chapter field, so ch 43 rests on the chapter page (eps 36, 38-39), the arc box (chs 42-45 = eps 36-39) and a beat match (Daisya walking out of the caved-in wall in front of Tyki). Ep 39's ch 44 is high — the episode restates ch 44 nearly page for page.

The stored fence ep 51 → 45 is repaired to 46 (evidence in repairs). If you take the repair, ep 51's chapters_adapted should become '44 (p16), 45 (p1-10), 46 (p2-10)' with volume 5; the stored partial{45-46} annotation and the 45/parity continue both remain correct.
